title: Database Migrations & Connection Pooling Handbook
summary: Quick revision notes on why schema migrations matter, Flyway versioned and repeatable migrations, Liquibase changelogs, why Hibernate ddl-auto is unsafe in production, and tuning HikariCP connection pools.

chapters.title: Schema Migrations: The Mental Model
points: Schema migration = versioned, ordered, scripted change to a database schema, kept in source control alongside application code
A migration tool records applied changes in a history table, so every environment (dev, CI, prod) converges to the same schema state
Migrations are forward-only and immutable: once applied, never edit the file; fix mistakes with a new migration
Core workflow: write a migration script, commit it, app or CI runs the tool on startup/deploy, the tool applies only pending scripts in order
Without migrations: manual SQL drift between environments, no audit trail, and unrepeatable deployments

chapters.title: Flyway: Versioned and Repeatable Migrations
points: Versioned migration: file V<version>__<description>.sql (e.g. V2__add_orders_table.sql); runs exactly once, in version order
Repeatable migration: file R__<description>.sql (no version); re-runs whenever its checksum changes, after all versioned ones, ordered by description
Naming rule: prefix V or R, then version, then TWO underscores, then description with underscores for spaces; a single underscore fails to match
Default location is classpath:db/migration; Spring Boot runs Flyway automatically on startup when flyway-core is on the classpath
flyway_schema_history table stores version, description, checksum, success flag; a changed checksum on an applied versioned file makes validate fail
Use repeatable migrations for views, stored procedures and functions (idempotent CREATE OR REPLACE); use versioned for tables and data changes

chapters.title: Flyway Ordering, Commands and Pitfalls
points: Versions compare numerically by segment (V1.10 comes after V1.2), not as strings; zero-padding is unnecessary
Out-of-order: a lower version added after a higher one was applied is rejected by default; flyway.outOfOrder=true allows it but risks inconsistent history
Core commands: migrate (apply pending), info (show status), validate (check checksums), repair (fix history table), baseline (mark an existing DB at a version), clean (drops everything)
baselineOnMigrate / baseline is how you adopt Flyway on an existing non-empty database
Never enable clean in production: set spring.flyway.clean-disabled=true (the default in recent versions)
Mistake: editing an applied migration causes a checksum mismatch; add a new versioned migration instead, and use repair only for deliberate fixes
Two developers using the same version number on different branches collide; agree on a numbering scheme such as timestamps

chapters.title: Liquibase Changelogs and Comparison with Flyway
points: Liquibase changelog is a master file (YAML, XML, JSON or SQL) that includes ordered changeSets
A changeSet is identified by id + author + file path; Liquibase records each in the DATABASECHANGELOG table with an MD5 checksum
changeSet example in YAML: changeSet: {id: 1, author: dev, changes: [createTable: {tableName: users}]}
Structured change types (createTable, addColumn) are database-agnostic and can generate rollback automatically; raw SQL changeSets need explicit rollback
Useful attributes: runOnChange (re-run when edited), runAlways, preconditions, and contexts/labels to target environments
DATABASECHANGELOGLOCK table prevents concurrent runs; a crashed run can leave it locked and need releasing
Flyway vs Liquibase: Flyway is plain SQL and simple, with versioned files in order; Liquibase is abstracted and declarative, with built-in rollback, preconditions and contexts

chapters.title: ddl-auto and Why Not in Production
points: spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto values: none, validate, update, create, create-drop
create drops and recreates the schema on startup; create-drop also drops it at shutdown; both destroy data
update only adds missing tables and columns; it never drops or renames columns, can't migrate data, and gives no history or review
Why not in production: unpredictable, unreviewable and unversioned DDL, no rollback, and risk of data loss or missing changes
Safe production setting: ddl-auto=validate (fail startup if the entities and schema differ) or none, with Flyway or Liquibase owning the schema
Acceptable use: create-drop or create with an in-memory database for quick prototypes and tests

chapters.title: HikariCP Connection Pooling and Cheat Sheet
points: Connection pooling reuses open database connections, because opening a connection per request is slow; HikariCP is the Spring Boot default pool

Key properties: maximumPoolSize (default 10), minimumIdle (defaults to maximumPoolSize, so the pool is fixed-size), connectionTimeout (default 30s wait for a connection), idleTimeout (10min), maxLifetime (30min)
Set maxLifetime a few seconds to minutes shorter than any database or firewall connection timeout, so Hikari retires connections first
Pool sizing: small is better; a common start is cores*2 + effective spindles, and total across app instances must stay below the database max_connections

Pool exhaustion symptom: 'Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms'; causes are leaked connections or long transactions, so release connections quickly and use leakDetectionThreshold to find leaks
Spring Boot config: spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size=10, spring.datasource.hikari.connection-timeout=30000
Cheat sheet: V__ versioned once / R__ repeatable on checksum change; migrate, info, validate, repair, baseline; prod ddl-auto=validate; never edit applied migrations
